LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard AUR `-git` package for an icon theme. It fetches from the package's own upstream GitHub repository (`https://github.com/erikdubois/surfn-arch-blue.git`) using the normal `git+https` source syntax, and `sha256sums=('SKIP')` and the unpinned VCS source are both ordinary, expected practices for `-git` packages. The `pkgver()` function only reads git metadata, and `package()` installs the theme into `${pkgdir}/usr/share/icons/` — standard packaging behavior.

The only mildly notable part is the `find "${_pkgname}" -type f \( -name '*.sh' -o -name 'icon-theme.cache' \) -delete` line, which removes shell scripts and icon caches from the theme directory before install. This is a hygiene choice scoped entirely to the package's own source tree (`$srcdir/Surfn-Arch-Blue/...`); the comment explains the caches are regenerated by the system icon-cache hook. Without `-L`, `find` does not follow symlinks, so it cannot escape the theme directory. There are no dangerous commands (`eval`, `base64`, `curl|bash`), no unexpected network targets, no exfiltration, no writes outside `${pkgdir}`, and no post-install hooks — nothing malicious.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard icon theme git package; no malicious behavior present.</summary>
</security_assessment>
